aspects.says: Every argument is evaluated before the method runs, whether or not the method uses it, so work that may not be needed is passed as a Supplier or a function.
basis: section:Every Argument Is Evaluated, Left to Right, Before the Method Runs

aspects.says: Recursion depth is limited by the bytes of the thread's stack, and interpreted frames are larger than compiled ones, so the same depth can fail just after start and succeed once warm.
basis: section:Each Call Holds a Stack Frame Until It Returns, So Recursion Depth Is Limited by the Stack

aspects.says: Data whose depth users control is walked with an explicit stack on the heap, which must carry what the recursion's frames held (the depth) and push children so they come off in order.
basis: section:Each Call Holds a Stack Frame Until It Returns, So Recursion Depth Is Limited by the Stack

aspects.says: An instance call runs the override of the object's class, chosen at run time, so behaviour that varies by subclass belongs in instance methods.
basis: section:An Instance Method Is Chosen by the Object; a Static Method by the Declared Type

aspects.says: The receiver is checked for null only after the expression before the dot and every argument, left to right, have been evaluated.
basis: section:Every Argument Is Evaluated, Left to Right, Before the Method Runs

aspects.says: A private method is not inherited, so a same-signature method in a subclass is a separate method and the declaring class's own calls keep using the private one.
basis: section:A Private Method Is Never Overridden, So the Class's Own Calls Keep Using It

aspects.says: A static call is bound at compile time to the declared type of the expression left of the dot; a subclass's static method hides the parent's, and a static call through null runs.
basis: section:An Instance Method Is Chosen by the Object; a Static Method by the Declared Type
